title: Stephen Hawking
about: the life of Stephen Hawking: when and where they were born, their best-known work, discovery or invention and when, a few moments from their life such as moving, studying or a turning point, and when they died if they have. Include several specific numbers, dates or names where the topic has them, some exact and some rounded or hedged (about, nearly, more than, up to).
passages: Stephen Hawking was born on 8 January 1942 in Oxford, England, exactly 300 years after the death of the astronomer Galileo. As a boy he took clocks and radios apart to see how they worked, though his school marks were only average. At 17 he went to study physics at Oxford, then moved to Cambridge to research the beginning of the universe. In 1963, when he was 21, doctors DIAGNOSED him with motor neuron disease and guessed he had about two years to live. Instead, he kept working for more than 50 years, and the illness slowly took away his ability to walk and speak.

In 1974 Hawking showed that black holes are not completely black. He worked out that they should slowly leak a faint glow, now called Hawking RADIATION, and might one day vanish. From 1979 he held a famous Cambridge post once held by Isaac Newton. Speaking through a computer voice, he wrote A Brief History of Time in 1988, and it sold more than 10 million copies around the world. He loved travel too, visiting places such as icy Antarctica and floating WEIGHTLESS on a special flight in 2007. This curious PHYSICIST died on 14 March 2018 in Cambridge, aged 76.
